task.question: What maximum distance did the crew of Artemis II reach from Earth on April 6, 2026?
task.evidence: April 6 – The crew of Artemis II breaks the record for the furthest humans have ever been from Earth, reaching a maximum distance of 252,756 miles (406,771 km) as they travel around the far side of the Moon.

Artemis II (April 1–11, 2026) flew a crew of four on a flyby of the Moon. It was the first crewed flight of the NASA-led Artemis program, the first beyond low Earth orbit (LEO) since Apollo 17 in 1972, and the first beyond LEO not part of the Apollo program. It was also the first crewed flight of the Space Launch System and of the Orion spacecraft, which the crew named Integrity.
The four crew members of Artemis II were Victor Glover, the only person of color, Christina Koch, the only woman, Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen the only person not from the United States, and Reid Wiseman the oldest person to travel beyond low Earth orbit and around the Moon. Orion flew around the Moon at a closest approach of about 4,067 miles (6,545 km; 3,534 nmi) from the far-side lunar surface at 23:00 UTC on April 6. Splashdown occurred April 11, 2026, 00:07:27 UTC (April 10, 5:07:27 p.m. PDT local time), in the Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego, California, where the U.S. Navy recovered the crew. It became the first crewed NASA mission to be recovered by the Navy since the Apollo–Soyuz Test Project in 1975.
